jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description:
About Code Metal

Code Metal is the leader in automated software engineering you can trust. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck in software has shifted from writing code to verifying it works, and AI cannot verify its own work with certainty. Code Metal takes a fundamentally different approach: constrain AI to what it does reliably, verify every step independently of the model using formal methods, and keep engineers in the loop on the decisions that matter. The result isn't code that probably works — it's code that is provably correct, with auditable proof. Customers including the U.S. Air Force, L3Harris, RTX, and Toshiba use Code Metal to modernize legacy code, optimize performance on real hardware, and move prototypes to production, fast. Founded in 2023 with offices in Boston and San Francisco, Code Metal is funded by Accel, Salesforce Ventures, B Capital, Smith Point Capital, J2 Ventures, Shield Capital, Overmatch, RTX, and others.

Learn more at codemetal.ai.

Code Metal is hiring its first Head of Product to own the company's product strategy, organization, and operating model. The Head of Product will sit at the intersection of Engineering, customers, and go-to-market and answer a fundamental question for the company's next phase.

The Head of Product will own the product layer built on top of Code Metal's core technical capabilities, including the continued evolution of our platform and the development of new products and experiences that make those capabilities accessible to customers. The mandate is to translate powerful underlying technology into products that solve clear customer problems, are easy to understand and adopt, and create natural paths to broader platform usage.

This person will report directly the CEO and the company's technical leadership to determine what products should be built on top of Code Metal's foundational technology, for whom, and in what sequence, while partnering closely with Sales to refine packaging, positioning, and the path from initial customer entry point to broader adoption.

The successful candidate will have done this before: taken differentiated foundational technology and built compelling products on top of it, creating the product experience, packaging, customer adoption, and commercial motion required to bring that technology to market.

What This Person Will Own:

Product Strategy & Vision: Define the product strategy for Code Metal's platform and establish a clear view of where the company will, and will not, invest.
Core Product Platform: Own the product direction and evolution of our platform and creating a coherent experience and roadmap across Code Metal's technical capabilities.
Zero-to-One Product Development: Work closely with Engineering to identify customer problems, develop new products and capabilities, validate them with customers, and take them from concept through market launch and adoption.
Customer Discovery: Build a disciplined approach to understanding engineering-led customers and translating their requirements into durable product insights rather than one-off feature requests.
Product Roadmap & Prioritization: Establish the mechanisms for making clear product and engineering tradeoffs across customer commitments, platform investments, technical debt, and long-term strategic opportunities.
Packaging & Commercialization: Determine how Code Metal's capabilities are organized, positioned, and packaged into products that customers can understand and purchase.
Go-to-Market Enablement: Partner tightly with Growth and Sales to create product narratives, use cases, demonstrations, competitive positioning, and technical enablement that make the platform easier to sell.
Sales Partnership: Participate directly in strategic customer conversations, particularly during the company's current stage, helping Sales understand customer requirements and helping customers understand the product's technical and business value.
Engineering Partnership: Serve as the primary product counterpart to Engineering and technical leadership, ensuring customer and market priorities are translated into clear product decisions without compromising technical integrity.
Product Organization: Build a high leverage, technically credible, high-output Product organization.

What we're looking for:

10+ years of B2B technology sales experience, including 5+ years leading scaled Product organizations.
A true builder who is comfortable starting with ambiguity, incomplete information, and an immature organizational structure.
Highly technical product executive. Must understand complex technical systems well to challenge assumptions, ask incisive questions, and partner with Code Metal's engineering organization.
Hands-on and comfortable operating without a large Product organization. This person should expect to personally conduct customer discovery, write product strategy, pressure-test requirements, support strategic deals, and drive prioritization.
Has strong product taste and can distinguish between a customer request, a repeatable product need, and a strategically important platform investment.
Commercially minded. Understands that great product leadership at Code Metal includes helping the company sell, package, and communicate its technology, not simply managing an engineering roadmap.
Comfortable making hard prioritization decisions and saying no when customer requests or internal initiatives do not support the broader product strategy.
Low ego and highly collaborative across Engineering, Growth, Sales, Solutions, and forward-deployed teams.
Has personally taken a deeply technical product from ground zero to market, rather than primarily inheriting mature products, established roadmaps, or functioning product organizations.
Has partnered closely with Sales to commercialize a product, including participating directly in customer conversations and learning what made the product sell, or fail to sell.
Has strong experience working with deeply technical engineering organizations and can earn credibility with engineers, architects, and technical founders.
Has translated emerging technical capabilities into products that can be repeatedly sold and deployed rather than remaining bespoke solutions.
Has experience establishing product-market fit, not simply scaling after product-market fit was already established.
Ideally has built products for developers, engineers, security teams, infrastructure teams, or other highly technical users.

Security is where the hardest problems in agentic AI now sit. An agent that can find a vulnerability, prove it reproduces, and patch it without breaking the system is doing work that takes a skilled human days. Measuring that honestly requires reproducible execution environments at scale and practitioners who have actually done the work. Make the strategic call on where Scale competes across the offense–defense spectrum — which capabilities we build training data for, which we only measure, and which we decline.

Amazon Music is hiring a Senior Manager, Product Management - Technical to serve as the Single Threaded Leader (STL) for Music Royalties and to lead the Partner Royalites, Payments and Experience organization. This role owns the full royalty payment ecosystem and is responsible for defining and expanding how Amazon Music partners with labels, publishers, and distributors across the partner lifecycle.

Amazon Music's partner ecosystem is growing in complexity and scale. Our label and publisher partners expect a seamless, modern experience to manage content, track performance, and receive accurate, timely payments. Today, the partner experience spans multiple internal teams — and this role will be responsible for defining the vision for a more unified partner interface, identifying opportunities to consolidate capabilities, and partnering across supply chain teams to deliver a cohesive experience.

This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of strategy, operations, and technology. You will lead an established organization while also shaping its future charter — evaluating where it makes sense to bring partner-facing capabilities under unified ownership and driving alignment across a complex stakeholder landscape. If you're energized by building on strong foundations, working across organizational boundaries, and creating experiences that earn trust with the biggest names in music — this role is for you.

This role reports into Music Licensing leadership and partners directly with Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Legal, Tax, and Content.

Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. From personalized music playlists to exclusive podcasts, concert livestreams to artist merch, Amazon Music is innovating at some of the most exciting intersections of music and culture. We offer experiences that serve all listeners with our different tiers of service: Prime members get access to all the music in shuffle mode, and top ad-free podcasts, included with their membership; customers can upgrade to Amazon Music Unlimited for unlimited, on-demand access to 100 million songs, including millions in HD, Ultra HD, and spatial audio; and anyone can listen for free by downloading the Amazon Music app or via Alexa-enabled devices. Join us for the opportunity to influence how Amazon Music engages fans, artists, and creators on a global scale. Learn more at https://www.amazon.com/music.

Royalties — Single Threaded Leader

Description

**The Opportunity**

95% of enterprise technology pilots deliver zero measurable P&L impact. The technology works — the gap is in the last mile: getting production systems running inside complex enterprises where legacy infrastructure, regulated data, and organizational complexity collide. AWS is making a billion-dollar investment in Forward Deployed Engineering ("FDE") to close that gap, and we're hiring product leaders who will define what we build and why.

This is a greenfield role. You'll build a product management practice, shape an entirely new category at AWS, and establish the engagement model that delivers delightful outcomes enabling customers to transform themselves.

**The Role**

As the Director of Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering will lead product management for FDE, building and leading the PM team that owns the end-to-end product lifecycle from customer engagement through production delivery through optimization and self-sufficiency. Your product managers embed directly inside enterprise customers — defining outcomes, writing specs, working hand-in-hand with engineering to ship production systems — and every engagement feeds back into AWS services and an underlying platform that makes the next one faster.

This is not a traditional AWS Product Management role. FDE product managers are field-facing: they live inside delivery, sit with customers, and turn engagement learnings into compounding platform value. You are the "CEO of the customer problem" — responsible for the *why* and *what*, while engineering owns the *how*.

Key job responsibilities

### Product Leadership

You own the customer outcomes. Your teams operate inside customer environments under real constraints and ambitious timelines — regulated data, brownfield infrastructure, multi-stakeholder governance. You lead the customer engagement strategy from the product side: define what a great pod PM does, allocate PM talent across engagements, ensure pods are solving the right problems, and hold executive customer relationships at the CIO/CTO level built on trust earned through delivered outcomes.

### Product & Platform Influence

You see what breaks across deployments and turn that into product direction. You influence AWS service roadmap from a position of earned authority because you've lived the deployment pain firsthand, and identify when custom pod work should graduate into platform primitives or native service capabilities.

You shape the FDE engagement model: how we scope, what we deliver, what we price, what we leave behind.

### Industry Practice & Productization

You build the domain expertise that compounds. Your teams develop industry-specific accelerators, reference architectures, and blueprints that generate pipeline for the next customer in your vertical. You define the use cases that feed qualification, pricing, and pod composition. You measure what matters: asset reuse rate, time-to-value, engagement velocity

### Go-to-Market Partnership

You partner with sales, specialists, and marketing to define pricing, packaging, and positioning. You own the commercial model for FDE engagements — how we price outcomes, what the customer buys, and how we demonstrate ROI. You build pipeline through customer stories, reference architectures

Experience with pricing, packaging, and go-to-market — having partnered with sales, marketing, and GTM teams to define commercial models and build pipeline
Executive presence with C-suite customers, earned through outcomes — can run a room with a VP/CTO and translate business problems into product requirements in real time

Experience delivering production systems inside large enterprise customer environments: regulated data, legacy infrastructure, organizational complexity, multi-party governance
Has built industry-specific solutions or vertical practices at scale — creating reusable assets that became a competitive moat

Description

We're building the future of cloud financial management, and the hardest unsolved problem in it is AI cost. Customers are moving from experimenting with generative AI to running it in production at scale. Spend is driven by tokens, model choice, inference patterns, and increasingly by agents that make their own consumption decisions. The AWS Billing organization processes millions of events per second to deliver the cost, usage, and optimization insights that power financial decisions at the world's largest enterprises. We are now extending that foundation to give customers the ability to understand, allocate, control, and optimize AI spend with the same rigor they apply to compute and storage today.

As Senior Manager, Product Management, you will own AWS's strategy for AI cost governance as a player-coach, personally driving the category-defining work while building the team that scales it. This is the highest-ambiguity, highest-leverage product space in the organization: the mechanics of tokenomics, attribution, and control for generative AI workloads are still being defined across the industry, and the decisions made here set the direction that partner service teams, enterprise customers, and eventually all industry players respond to. You will personally own the product bets that define the category, hire and develop the product managers who help you carry that ownership as it grows, and set the technical direction that other product managers across Billing and partner teams build against.

In this role, you will define what it means to govern AI spend on AWS: how cost is attributed at the token, model, and agent level; how customers allocate that cost to teams, applications, and business units; and how they set and enforce controls before spend, rather than explaining it afterward. You will write the strategy documents and PR/FAQs for the most consequential launches, run the customer conversations, and make the hard trade-off calls on scope, sequencing, and where AWS should lead versus follow — doing this work yourself on the bets that matter most, and coaching your team to take on more of it as they grow into it. You will pressure-test metering, API, and interface designs directly with engineering, and dig into consumption data and customer telemetry to understand where the real cost drivers and governance gaps are. You will own the measurement of whether these capabilities actually change customer behavior, including adoption, spend under active governance, and the degree to which cost visibility unblocks AI expansion, and build the review mechanisms — run by you and the product managers you develop — that hold the organization accountable to it.

You will make the calls on how AI cost governance extends to emerging surfaces, including foundation model inference, agentic workloads, and third-party and marketplace model consumption, and on when AWS should build new primitives versus extend existing cost management constructs. You will partner with engineering leaders, applied science leaders, and product leaders across Bedrock, AgentCore, and the broader AWS generative AI portfolio to ensure cost governance is designed in rather than retrofitted, and you will drive alignment on strategy and investment across multiple organizations without owning the teams that execute it. You will represent this product area to senior AWS leadership, enterprise CFOs and FinOps practitioners, and industry analysts, and you will shape how the market thinks about the economics of running AI in production.

This role requires deep technical judgment, comfort operating with incomplete information on problems that have no precedent, the influence to move organizations you do not control, and the discipline to both do the work yourself and develop the people who will eventually own it without you. If you are excited about defining a product category that does not yet exist — and about the fact that every enterprise scaling generative AI will eventually need what you build — this role offers the opportunity to set AWS's position on the economics of AI.

Build the mechanisms your team uses to engage customers across channels and serve as the voice of the customer inside AWS.

Establish how customer feedback flows into product decisions, and use it to make the calls on where the team invests.

Own the full product lifecycle across your team's surface area, from strategic planning through tactical execution.

Define the goals, input metrics, and output metrics that measure success for the product experience.

Write and deliver the updates that go to VP and SVP audiences on the products, key launches, and strategic bets. Coach your PMs on the writing and communication skills that get their work to the same bar.

Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing PM team. Set the bar for product excellence, give direct feedback, and grow PMs into the next level.

Description

The AI Center of Excellence builds shared AI building blocks - primitives - that change how Amazon's systems work, not what features they ship. We take on the hardest problems first, prove each primitive with one partner on one real problem, then open it up so any team at Amazon can adopt what we've validated without solving it again.

We are looking for a Product Manager - Technical who can own the vision and lifecycle of these primitives, drive them from concept through adoption, and make sound product and technical trade-offs in a fast-moving AI domain.

Key job responsibilities

Own the product lifecycle for AI primitives end-to-end - from customer discovery and problem framing through vision definition, roadmap prioritization, execution with cross-team dependencies, launch, and post-launch performance optimization
Define product strategy by understanding problems that cut across multiple teams and personas - translating that into clear principles, requirements, and roadmap priorities that sequence work on evidence
Drive adoption by partnering with early adopters, generalizing requirements from multiple contexts, and ensuring primitives work for any team without requiring your team to operate them
Evaluate technical proposals alongside scientists and ML engineers - understanding architecture trade-offs and balancing feature delivery with system health and long-term maintainability
Make crisp product decisions in ambiguous AI/ML domains where the problem and strategy may not yet be defined - using data, customer insight, and judgment
